method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: The Criminal Code (Appendix B to the Criminal Code Act Compilation Act 1913), compilation from legislation.wa.gov.au (law 196, mrdoc 49336, retrieved 7 September 2026); no compilation number stated; latest amendment in the compilation table (Education and Care Services National Law Application Act 2026 Pt 6 Div 7) in force 1 May 2026; uncommenced Prostitution Amendment Act 2008 s 30, Evidence Act 2025 Pt 12 Div 10 and Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Act 2025 Pt 17 Div 5 not shown; no regulations set a number used ($1 000, $10 000, $50 000 and the fines are the Code's own)
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is reproduced under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution in ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: The Criminal Code ss 5(1)-(3) (summary trial), 7 (principal offenders), 22 (honest claim of right), 29 (immature age), 80I and 221 (racial and other aggravation), 338, 338A, 338B (threats), 370, 371 (stealing), 378 (penalty for stealing and special cases), 426, 426A (summary penalty for stealing), 444, 445 (criminal damage, damaging property); the rest of the Code left out
seat: the accused person (Jake at 15, charged with stealing) and the victim of threats and criminal damage (Jake at 29)
